decisions.reason: The dispensing-flow decision concerns pour sequencing and sputtering, not the quality produced by the mixing process; the separate mixing-quality clause already has its own same-message Event.
Clean dispensing flow does not change food-path cleaning requirements, and the source message's separate cleaning clause is already represented by a same-message Event.

The client reaffirms the already-selected solenoid approach; the new clean, seamless, non-sputtering criteria concern flow quality and do not change the existing valve mechanism or button-actuation behavior.
The message repeats existing no-drip and leak-prevention constraints without changing them; the source Event's new non-sputtering and dispensing-sequence values are separate flow-quality criteria.
Sputtering during dispensing is distinct from splashing during mixing, and the source message's separate splash-control changes are already represented by a same-message Event.
The dispensing-flow decision does not determine whisk material, style, size, or positioning; the source message's separate whisk uncertainty is already represented.
Clean, seamless, non-sputtering flow does not necessarily change the spout's existing location, orientation, geometry reference, or fabrication style.
The dispensing sequence and sputtering constraint do not change bowl capacity, form, size reference, or refill policy.
The client retains the solenoid approach but does not change the existing custom-spout strategy or the broader off-the-shelf component policy.
The dispensing-flow criteria do not alter the power source, battery policy, or electrical architecture.
The source establishes dispensing quality criteria but does not change the general repeated-operation or event-use reliability requirement.
Reviewing possible BOM adjustments does not change the BOM deliverable itself; the source Event only modifies product dispensing behavior.
